questions.question_text: All of the below options apply symptoms are more commonly in depression linked to learning disability than in those of normal intelligence with the exception of

options.text: Deterioration and regression in previously acquired social competencies

correct_answer.text: Hypochondriasis

questions.explanation: Though most symptoms of depression seen in learning disabled individuals are same as those seen in general population, certain differences exist. Cognitive syndrome of depression including memory disturbance and loss of concentration are often not detected. Similarly, guilt and recurrent thoughts of suicide are under-reported. But biological changes associated with depression such as psychomotor retardation, disturbed sleep, appetite and weight loss and diurnal variation in symptoms are more readily detected. Some symptoms may be more marked in depressed individuals with severe learning disability e.g. psychomotor agitation, irritability and behavioural disturbance. Decline in established activities of daily living and tearfulness may be signs of hidden depression in some patients. Hypochondriasis and other formed beliefs are rarely seen. Prasher V. Presentation and management of depression in people with learning disability. Advances in Psychiatric Treatment 1999; 5: 447–454.

questions.question_text: The DSM-5 diagnosis of intellectual developmental disorder encompasses severity specifiers—Mild, Moderate, Severe, and Profound—with which to indicate the level of supports required in various domains of adaptive behavior. which of the following options features would not be characteristic of an patients with a “Severe” level of impairment?

options.text: The patients generally has little understanding of written language or of concepts involving numbers, quantity, time, and money.
The patients’s spoken language is quite limited in terms of vocabulary and grammar.
The patients requires support for all activities of daily living, encompassing meals, dressing, bathing, and toileting.
In adulthood, the patients may be able to sustain competitive employment in a job that does not emphasize conceptual skills.
The patients cannot make responsible decisions regarding the well-being of self or others.

correct_answer.text: In adulthood, the patients may be able to sustain competitive employment in a job that does not emphasize conceptual skills.

questions.explanation: Competitive employment may be attainable by individuals with a “Mild” level of impairment but would not be characteristic of those with a “Severe” level of impairment. Intellectual disability (intellectual developmental disorder) is a disorder with onset during the developmental period that includes both intellectual and adaptive functioning deficits in conceptual, social, and practical domains (DSM-5 Table 1, pp. 34–36). The conceptual (academic) domain involves competence in memory, language, reading, writing, math reasoning, acquisition of practical knowledge, problem solving, and judgment in novel situations, among others. The social domain involves awareness of others’ thoughts, feelings, and experiences; empathy; interpersonal communication skills; friendship abilities; and social judgment, among others. The practical domain involves learning and self-management across life settings, including personal care, job responsibilities, money management, recreation, self-management of behavior, and school and work task organization, among others.

questions.question_text: Blood levels of which of the following substances has been adversely linked to IQ of a child?

questions.explanation: Lead is established to have neurotoxic effects on growing brain; blood lead concentrations above 10 μg per decilitre (0.483 μmol per litre) are associated with adverse intellectual functioning and social–behavioural conduct. A blood lead concentration of 10 μg per decilitre or higher is designated as a ‘level of concern’ by the World Health Organization. It is estimated that a loss of 7.4 IQ points takes place with a lifetime average blood lead concentration of up to 10 μg per decilitre. Canfi eld RL, Henderson CR Jr, Cory-Slechta DA, et al. Intellectual Impairment in Children with Blood Lead Concentrations below 10 μg per decilitre. New England Journal of Medicine 2003; 348: 1517–1526.

questions.question_text: The point prevalence of schizophrenia in people with learning disability is
questions.explanation: The point prevalence of schizophrenia is estimated to be between 3% and 4% in the learning-disabled population compared with 1% in the general population. Schizophrenia cannot be reliably diagnosed below an IQ of approximately 45. Often in clinical practice, if there is evidence of delusions or hallucinations in those with profound learning disability, a diagnosis of psychosis not otherwise specifi ed is used. Despite this the rate of schizophrenia is signifi cantly higher among the population with learning disability. This increase is seen despite the overall rate of psychiatric illness among adults with mild to moderate learning disability being similar to that in the general adult population without learning disability. The reason for this increased comorbidity is unclear, and common underlying brain damage that could cause both learning disability and schizophrenia cannot be ruled out. Deb S, Thomas M and Bright C. Mental disorder in adults with intellectual disability. 1. Prevalence of functional psychiatric illness among a community-based population aged between 16 and 64 years. Journal of Intellectual Disability Research 2001; 45: 495–505.

correct_answer.text: Generally independent with self-care

questions.explanation: The source explicitly states that individuals with mild learning disability are generally independent with self-care, distinguishing them from more severe forms that require varying levels of supervision or nursing care.

questions.question_text: Living arrangements most appropriate for adults with severe learning disability are described as which of the following?

options.text: Supervised living situations, such as group homes

correct_answer.text: Supervised living situations, such as group homes

questions.explanation: That Adults with severe LD can adapt well to supervised living situations, such as group homes, and may be able to perform work-related tasks under supervision.

questions.question_text: Which adaptive functioning domains are typically preserved in mild learning disability?

options.text: Communications, self-care, social skills, work, leisure, and safety

correct_answer.text: Communications, self-care, social skills, work, leisure, and safety

questions.explanation: That The adaptive functions of people with mild LD are effective in several areas, such as communications, self-care, social skills, work, leisure, and safety.

questions.question_text: What is the male-to-female ratio of learning disability prevalence mentioned in the source?
questions.explanation: The source explicitly states that LD is around 1.5 times more common among men than women, establishing a 1.5:1 male-to-female ratio.

questions.question_text: The correlation between learning disability severity and psychiatric comorbidity suggests that:

options.text: Mild LD has the highest psychiatric burden
Psychiatric problems are unrelated to LD severity
Greater severity of LD correlates with higher risk of mental health problems
Only moderate LD shows psychiatric comorbidity
Psychiatric symptoms always indicate additional diagnosis

correct_answer.text: Greater severity of LD correlates with higher risk of mental health problems

questions.explanation: The prevalence of psychopathology seems to be correlated with the severity of LD; the greater the severity of LD, the higher the risk of mental health problems.

questions.question_text: What is the prevalence range of learning disability in the general population?
questions.explanation: The source clearly states The prevalence of LD is estimated to range from 1-3% of the population. This is a straightforward factual recall question. ---

questions.question_text: At which age range is the incidence of learning disability highest, according to the source?

correct_answer.text: 10-14 years

questions.explanation: The source identifies that The highest incidence is in school-age children, with the peak at ages 10 to 14 years.

questions.question_text: In which psychiatric comorbidity are individuals with mild learning disability more likely to present?

correct_answer.text: Disruptive and conduct-disorder behaviours

questions.explanation: The source explicitly states that Disruptive and conduct-disorder behaviours occurred more commonly in the people with a mild LD, whereas severe LD has higher rates of autism spectrum disorder.

questions.question_text: Individuals with profound learning disability requiring nursing care typically demonstrate which characteristic?

options.text: Comprehension and use of language that is very limited
Independence in self-care with minimal support
Academic skills up to third-grade level

correct_answer.text: Comprehension and use of language that is very limited

questions.explanation: Profound LD as having Comprehension and use of language very limited and requiring nursing care or 'life support' and assistance with most ADL. Options A, B, D, and E do not apply to profound LD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is classified as a genetic factor contributing to learning disability?

correct_answer.text: Down syndrome (autosomal chromosome disorder)

questions.explanation: Down syndrome is explicitly listed under Autosomal chromosome disorders in the genetic factors section. All other options represent environmental factors (prenatal, perinatal, or postnatal).

questions.question_text: Which genetic factor is specifically mentioned as an autosomal chromosome disorder causing learning disability?

correct_answer.text: Down's syndrome

questions.explanation: The source explicitly lists Autosomal chromosome disorders like Down's syndrome as a genetic factor causing learning disability. The other options are either X-linked (hemophilia, colour blindness, Fragile X) or autosomal recessive (Duchenne muscular dystrophy) but are not mentioned as primary examples in the autosomal chromosome disorder category.

questions.question_text: The Vineland Adaptive Behaviour Scale is used to measure which of the following?

correct_answer.text: Adaptive functioning

questions.explanation: The source specifically identifies the Vineland Adaptive Behaviour Scale as a standardized scale used to measure adaptive functioning, which refers to how effectively individuals cope with common life demands.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best explains why the majority of individuals with moderate learning disability have an identifiable organic aetiology, whereas this is less commonly documented in mild learning disability?

options.text: Mild LD is entirely genetic in origin
Moderate and severe LD typically result from significant developmental insults, while mild LD may result from polygenic or environmental factors with less obvious organic pathology
Organic causes only affect moderate LD
Mild LD is never caused by organic factors
Organic aetiologies resolve by adulthood in mild LD

correct_answer.text: Moderate and severe LD typically result from significant developmental insults, while mild LD may result from polygenic or environmental factors with less obvious organic pathology

questions.explanation: That Majority have an identifiable organic aetiology for moderate LD but does not make the same statement for mild LD. This pattern reflects the clinical observation that more severe disabilities often have identifiable organic causes (infections, trauma, genetic syndromes), while milder presentations may arise from more subtle polygenetic or environmental contributions less readily identified on investigation.

questions.question_text: According to epidemiological data, learning disability is more common in which gender?

options.text: Approximately 1.5 times more common in males
Three times more common in males

correct_answer.text: Approximately 1.5 times more common in males

questions.explanation: LD is around 1.5 times more common among men than women. This is a specific epidemiological finding. ---

questions.question_text: Rubella infection in early pregnancy is associated with learning disability as which type of aetiological factor?

correct_answer.text: External prenatal factor

questions.explanation: The source lists rubella under External prenatal factors - particularly in the early stages of pregnancy, specifically naming it as an infection that can contribute to LD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the relationship between learning disability severity and psychiatric comorbidity?

options.text: Higher severity correlates with lower mental health problems
Higher severity correlates with higher risk of mental health problems
Only mild LD has psychiatric comorbidity
Psychiatric comorbidity only occurs in profound LD

correct_answer.text: Higher severity correlates with higher risk of mental health problems

questions.explanation: The source explicitly states that The prevalence of psychopathology seems to be correlated with the severity of LD; the greater the severity of LD, the higher the risk of mental health problems including mood disorders, schizophrenia, ADHD, and conduct disorder.

questions.question_text: What percentage of children and adults with learning disability have comorbid mental health problems?

correct_answer.text: Up to 2/3

questions.explanation: The source clearly states Epidemiological surveys indicate that up to 2/3 children and adults with LD have comorbid mental health problems. This is a direct factual recall question. ---

questions.question_text: According to the epidemiological data, what is the approximate percentage of the learning disability population with severe or profound learning disability combined?
questions.explanation: That severe LD comprises 4% and profound LD comprises 1–2% of the learning disability population, totalling approximately 5–6% when combined.

questions.question_text: When compared with the general population, the range of full-scale IQ in people with Turner's syndrome is shifted down by

correct_answer.text: 0 points

questions.explanation: Learning disability is rare in Turner's syndrome. But note that verbal-performance dissociation can be seen.

questions.question_text: The commonest cardiac malformation seen in Down's syndrome is

correct_answer.text: Endocardial cushion defect

questions.explanation: Congenital heart defects are common in Down (40-50%); they are frequently observed in patients with Down syndrome who are hospitalized (62%) and are a common cause of death in this aneuploidy in the first 2 years of life. The most common congenital heart defects are endocardial cushion defect (43%), ventricular septal defect (32%), secundum atrial septal defect (10%), tetralogy of Fallot (6%), and isolated patent ductus arteriosus (4%). PDA is seen in 16% while pulmonary stenosis in 9% (http://emedicine.medscape.com/article/943216-overview).
